title: 2.3 Postulates and Diagrams

icans: I can identify and use postulates about points, lines, and planes.
I can sketch a diagram from a description.
I can tell what I can and cannot assume from a diagram.

vocab: a rule that is ___________ without proof
a line that meets a plane in a point and is perpendicular to every line in the plane __________ that point

blocks.sec: Part 1 · Discovery: why doesn’t a stool wobble?

head: Question
What we found
rows: How many lines go through two points?
How many planes go through three points that are not on a line?
Why can a four-legged table wobble but a three-legged stool can’t?

blocks.sec: Part 2 · Notes and examples (fill in each note, then work the example)

notes: Two Point Postulate: through any two points there is exactly _______________ line. Plane Intersection Postulate: if two planes intersect, their intersection is a _______________.

blocks.stem:
Which postulate does each statement illustrate?
a.  Points A and B lie on exactly one line.
b.  Planes P and Q meet in line ℓ.

notes: Three Point Postulate: through any three _______________ points there is exactly one plane.

blocks.stem: Explain why a three-legged stool never wobbles, using a postulate.
Sketch: line ℓ is perpendicular to plane P at point A, and ray AB lies in plane P.

notes: Reading diagrams: you CAN assume points are collinear and angles are adjacent or vertical as drawn. You CANNOT assume segments or angles are _______________ or that lines are perpendicular unless it is marked.

blocks.stem:
Use the diagram. Which statements can you assume?
a.  A, E, and C are collinear.
b.  ∠AEB and ∠BEC are adjacent.
c.  ∠AEB is a right angle.
d.  AE = EC
A student says, “A̅E̅ ≅ E̅C̅ because they look the same length in the diagram.” What is wrong?
Which postulate? “Through points P, Q, and R, which are not on one line, there is exactly one plane.”
Two lines cross at point E in a diagram with no marks. Can you assume the angles across from each other are vertical angles? Can you assume they are right angles?

tickets.stem: If two planes intersect, what is their intersection?
Can you assume two segments are congruent from a diagram with no marks?
How many lines go through two points?
